tiers_code_only.purpose: Cross-subject comprehension-score comparator. The 'tiers' figure above is denominated over all 3,767,918 lines, which is dominated by 3,291,902 lines of bundled curriculum/ML JSON classified 'data' (see size.note). A number driven by the size of bundled data blobs makes this subject look overwhelmingly detect-only when its actual authored code is mostly full-parsing languages, and would poison any comparison against a subject with a smaller or absent data payload. This field restricts the same tier partition to lines_by_class=='code' only (342,177 lines), excluding 'data', 'docs' (130,253 lines), and 'config' (3,586 lines).
tiers_code_only.denominator_definition: size.lines_by_class.code, i.e. lines in files the analyzer classifies 'code' (analyzer/derive/pipeline.py:_file_line_class), excluding data/docs/config.
tiers_code_only.note: Full-parse languages (swift/python/rust/typescript/javascript/ruby/cpp) occur only in the 'code' class under the analyzer's own classifier, so the full-parse LINE COUNT is unchanged from the all-lines figure above (330,946 either way); only the denominator shrinks, from 3,767,918 all-lines to 342,177 code-lines, which moves the full-parse SHARE from 8.7833% to 96.7178% (+87.9345 percentage points). The all-lines 'tiers' object above is not wrong, but it answers 'what share of everything shipped is full-parse', while this object answers 'what share of the authored code is full-parse' -- the latter is the fair comparator across subjects with different amounts of bundled data. The prior version of this file's 'tiers.note' said this narrower split could not be measured without recomputing from raw source; it has now been computed from the same mirrored dataset by reading the per-file path/language/size_bytes already present in each of the 254 component detail shards (which the manifest itself does not expose as a flat cross-tab) and classifying each file with the analyzer's own _file_line_class function, imported as a library rather than reimplemented. Fidelity check: summing this per-file classification over all 1,249 unique files (deduplicated from 1,328 raw entries, since a file can be listed under more than one component) reproduces size.lines_by_class exactly -- code=342177, config=3586, data=3291902, docs=130253, sum=3767918 -- confirming the per-file records and the manifest's own aggregate agree.
tiers_code_only.provenance: python3 script run from /Volumes/Studio/dev/solution-explorer (repo root, for the analyzer import) reading /Volumes/Studio/dev/.evidence/solution-explorer/mirrors/20260819/site/architecture/data/detail-*.json (254 shards): collected every files[] entry (path, language, lines, size_bytes) into a dict keyed by path (dedup, 1249 unique of 1328 raw entries, no value conflicts on the 50 duplicated paths); imported analyzer.derive.pipeline._file_line_class(path, language, size_bytes) unmodified and applied it per file; verified sum-by-class against architecture/manifest.json stats.lines_by_class (exact match); restricted to class=='code' and partitioned those 342,177 lines by tier_determination's full_parse/detect_only language sets.

language_mix.note: Full-parse vs detect-only is dominated by the JSON data payload (see size.note): json alone is 87.2% of all lines and is detect-only, which pulls the detect-only share to 91.2%. Restricted to lines_by_class 'code'+'docs'+'config' (476,016 lines, excluding the 'data' class), the mix would read very differently. See tiers_code_only above for the code-only split (data/docs/config excluded), which is the figure to use for cross-subject comparisons.

tier_determination.method: Current tier membership was read directly from analyzer source, not from prose docs, per task instruction: the parser registry at analyzer/parsers/__init__.py (PARSERS = {swift, python, rust, typescript, javascript, go, java, ruby, csharp, cpp, storyboard}, each with a working extract_symbols/extract_imports) cross-referenced against the authoritative FULL_PARSE_LANGS set asserted by tests/test_language_tiers.py (Swift, Python, Rust, TypeScript/JavaScript, Go, Ruby, Java, C#, C/C++), which exists specifically to keep the docs and the parser registry from drifting apart. Storyboard/xib has a registered parser but is explicitly commented in __init__.py as 'always regex-tier (no tree-sitter)' schema-detection, and is excluded from FULL_PARSE_LANGS by that test, so it is classified detect-only here, matching the test's authoritative list rather than the raw PARSERS dict.
tier_determination.confirms_java_csharp_cpp_move: tests/test_language_tiers.py's own docstring states the prior state directly: 'Both README.md and PROJECT-OVERVIEW.md listed Java, C# and C/C++ as detection + metrics only while analyzer/parsers/ carried full regex AND tree-sitter parsers for all three... This test keeps the tables and the parsers honest with each other.' Java and C# have zero lines in this particular dataset's language stats, so their tier placement could not be cross-checked against real data here, but their parser registration (analyzer/parsers/java.py, analyzer/parsers/csharp.py, both in PARSERS) is unconditional, not dataset-dependent.
